kind: VISUAL DESIGN REVIEW BY AGENT / NOT REAL USER TESTING
method: Actual screenshot images inspected using the image viewer; browser layout measurements are recorded separately.
observations: All seven 1440x900 pages retain readable hierarchy, consistent navigation, neutral light surfaces and restrained teal actions.
Center at 1280 retains six information groups, visible filters and pagination; no full-page horizontal overflow.
Detail is a continuous investigation document: version, risk, remediation, evidence, relations and factual timeline. Long content scrolls naturally.
Review candidates remain side by side at 1280; scope, original excerpts, human choice and reason stay visible. Final submit is below the initial fold and accessible by vertical scroll.
Asset inventory shows affected, unknown and not-affected-for-one-vulnerability as distinct states.
Evidence drawer groups source excerpts, scope, published/retrieved time and lineage; abstract claim status stays separate from severity.
Assistant renders fixed mock results beside public tool summaries and clickable citations. Timeout retains partial results and an explicit retry.
All screens clearly label mock data. Source success/failure and historical last-success times are independent; no fake benchmark performance.
corrections: Merged fragmented detail section cards into a continuous white document.
Replaced internal source IDs with readable names where appropriate.
Added candidate values and distinct deferred state to simulated review history.
Retained accessible navigation names at tablet width.
Waited for prior transient toast to disappear before capturing the timeout screenshot.
remaining: No unresolved obvious desktop clipping found in inspected mock screenshots.
Real long evidence, source names, asset inventories and production density need another pass with live data.
Full multiselect/date popovers, screen-reader behavior, other browsers/fonts and zoom remain production frontend verification tasks.
Mobile and dark mode are not priority deliverables in this phase.
